exercise.name: Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank

reference.title: Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Dynamic plank (anti-extension, anti-rotation) with elbow extension
exercise.laterality: Alternating lead arm (both sides in one loop)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you press up to the hands, breathe in as you lower to the forearms; never hold the breath for long.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up and 2 s down

prescription.tempo: Steady, about 2 s up and 2 s down
prescription.progression: Feet closer together, slower reps, or a pause in each position

cues.text: Forearm plank: elbows under the shoulders, feet hip width or wider, body in one line.
Place the right hand under the right shoulder and press up, then the left: up to a high plank.
High plank: hands under the shoulders, arms straight, hips level.
Lower to the right forearm, then the left, back to the forearm plank.
Lead with the left arm this time: left hand, then right, up to the hands.
Left forearm down, then the right.

mistakes.fix: Widen the feet and brace; the hips stay as level as you can keep them.

mistakes.mistake: Hips piking up during the transitions
mistakes.fix: Keep one line from the shoulders to the heels.

mistakes.mistake: Hands placed far ahead of the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Plant each hand right under its shoulder.
Move one arm at a time with control.

kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees on the forearms to nearly straight on the hands (clinical opinion)
Rises by about one forearm length between the two planks (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈13° off straight in the high plank
kinematics.norm: Held straight in both planks (Schoenfeld 2014 set-up for the forearm plank)

kinematics.peak: Shoulder line tilts ≈34° with one hand and one forearm down (feet 21 cm apart)
kinematics.norm: Some roll toward the lowered side is unavoidable while one arm is up; a wider stance keeps it small (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: About 2 s up, 0.4 s high plank, 2 s down per rep, lead arm alternating

sources.title: GymVisual #8964, Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank, video (movement reference; page not readable here)

Schoenfeld et al. 2014, an electromyographic comparison of a modified version of the plank with a long lever and posterior tilt versus the traditional plank exercise (Sports Biomechanics, doi 10.1080/14763141.2014.942355)

Ekstrom, Donatelli and Carp 2007, electromyographic analysis of core trunk, hip and thigh muscles during 9 rehabilitation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 37(12):754-762; PubMed 18560185)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low back pain that increases in the plank: shorten the hold or drop to the knee plank.
High blood pressure: breathe steadily; long breath-held efforts raise blood pressure.
Wrist pain on the hands: use fists or push-up handles, or stay on the forearms.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: hands together (forearms in a slight V) or an incline plank with the forearms on a bench.
Elbow discomfort: fold the mat under the forearms.
regressions: Static forearm and high planks held separately.

muscleNotes.core: Abdominals hold the plank line while the support shifts from two forearms to one hand and one forearm and back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Obliques resist the rotation each time one arm leaves the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Obliques resist the rotation each time one arm leaves the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Triceps straighten the elbow to press up from the forearm to the hand (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Triceps straighten the elbow to press up from the forearm to the hand (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Elbow: 90 on the forearms, straight on the hands
